title: The TAR binding dynamics and its implication in Tat degradation mechanism.
authors: Ning, Shangbo; Zeng, Chengwei; Zeng, Chen; Zhao, Yunjie
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子加速采样MD研究HIV Tat/TAR/P-TEFb复合物中蛋白-RNA结合动态及抑制剂作用机制，虽为蛋白-RNA而非TF-DNA体系，但蛋白-核酸互作动态建模方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a retrovirus that progressively attacks the human immune system. It is known that the HIV viral protein Tat recruits the host elongation factor, positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb), onto the nascent HIV viral transactivation response element (TAR) RNA to overcome the elongation pause for active transcription of the entire viral genome. Interestingly, there exists an amplifying feedback loop between Tat and TAR-a reduction in Tat increases the elongation pause, resulting in more TAR RNA fragments instead of the entire viral genome transcript, and the TAR fragments as a scaffold for PRC2 complex in turn promote Tat ubiquitination and degradation. In this study, the structural ensembles and binding dynamics of various interfaces in the Tat/TAR/P-TEFb complex are probed by all-atom accelerated sampling molecular dynamics simulations. The results show that a protein-binding inhibitor F07#13 targeting the Tat/P-TEFb interface initiates the above feedback loop and shuts down the active transcription. Another RNA binding inhibitor, JB181, targeting the Tat/TAR interface, can prevent TAR from pulling down the Tat from P-TEFb protein and further reducing Tat degradation. The detailed mechanism of the complex dynamics helps elucidate how Tat and TAR coordinate the regulation between HIV genome transcription versus possible HIV latency.
abstract_zh: 人类免疫缺陷病毒（HIV）是一种逆转录病毒，逐步攻击人体免疫系统。已知HIV病毒蛋白Tat将宿主延伸因子——正转录延伸因子b（P-TEFb）——招募到新生HIV病毒反式激活反应元件（TAR）RNA上，以克服延伸暂停，实现整个病毒基因组的活跃转录。有趣的是，Tat与TAR之间存在一个放大反馈回路——Tat的减少会增加延伸暂停，导致更多TAR RNA片段而非整个病毒基因组转录本产生，而作为PRC2复合物支架的TAR片段反过来促进Tat的泛素化和降解。在本研究中，通过全原子加速采样分子动力学模拟，探测了Tat/TAR/P-TEFb复合物中各种界面的结构集合和结合动力学。结果表明，靶向Tat/P-TEFb界面的蛋白结合抑制剂F07#13启动了上述反馈回路并关闭了活跃转录。另一种靶向Tat/TAR界面的RNA结合抑制剂JB181，可以阻止TAR从P-TEFb蛋白中拉下Tat，并进一步减少Tat降解。复合物动力学的详细机制有助于阐明Tat和TAR如何协调HIV基因组转录与可能的HIV潜伏期之间的调控。
